memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will drive you and the king you set over you to a nation unknown to you or your ancestors. There you will worship other gods, gods of wood and stone. You will become a thing of horror, a byword and an object of ridicule among all the peoples where the Lord will drive you... You will sow much seed in the field but you will harvest little, because locusts will devour it." — Deut 28:36-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the curse reaches toward exile — being driven from the promised land to a foreign nation. This is one of the most significant warnings in the chapter, because it actually came to pass centuries later when Israel and Judah were carried off into captivity. God's word proved true. The exile stands as sober evidence that these warnings were not empty threats.

Yet even here, in the very heart of judgment, we can trace threads of hope if we know the rest of the story. The God who warned of exile also promised, again and again through His prophets, that He would one day gather His scattered people and bring them home. Judgment was never God's final word to His people.

For us, this points to a beautiful gospel truth. We too were once "scattered" — far off, strangers to God, wandering in a kind of spiritual exile. But in Christ, "you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ" (Eph 2:13). The Good Shepherd came to gather His scattered sheep and bring them home to the Father.

So even the darkest warning in Scripture ultimately serves the story of redemption. The God who scatters in judgment is the God who gathers in mercy. And in Jesus, the wanderer is welcomed home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I remember that I was once "far off" before God brought me near?
2. How does the fulfilment of these warnings show me God's word is true?
3. How does it comfort me that God gathers His scattered people home?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that though I was once far off, You brought me near through the blood of Christ. You are the God who gathers Your people home. Keep me close to You always. Amen.
